report_name: Ransomware Attacks in Japan Rise; 'The Gentlemen' Group Dominates

threat_actors.name: The Gentlemen
threat_actors.description: The most active ransomware group targeting Japan in the first half of 2026, responsible for 14 incidents. The group operates a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model, employs double-extortion tactics, and primarily targets small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs). Linguistic evidence suggests potential involvement of Russian-speaking individuals.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion of small-to-medium enterprises in Japan through ransomware and data leak threats.

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: An active ransomware group targeting Japan, responsible for seven incidents in the first half of 2026.

threat_actors.name: SafePay
threat_actors.description: An active ransomware group targeting Japan, responsible for seven incidents in the first half of 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Gained initial access through exploiting vulnerabilities in public-facing services such as VPNs and RDP.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Used phishing campaigns as an initial access vector.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Encrypted files on both individual Windows systems and virtual machines on VMware ESXi servers to cause widespread impact.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Deleted backups to inhibit recovery from the ransomware attack.

attack_patterns.name: SSH
attack_patterns.description: Used SSH to connect to VMware ESXi hosts, likely for lateral movement and execution of malicious commands.

malware.name: Qilin
malware.description: Ransomware used by the Qilin group in attacks targeting organizations in Japan.

tools.name: Cobalt Strike
tools.description: Used for lateral movement within victim networks.

tools.name: PsExec
tools.description: Mentioned as a legitimate software often abused by ransomware attackers.

tools.name: esxcli
tools.description: A command-line utility on VMware ESXi hosts used by attackers to manipulate and kill virtual machine processes.

identities.name: small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs)
identities.description: The primary target of ransomware groups in Japan, accounting for 80% of all victims. Defined as organizations with capital under JPY 1 billion.

infrastructure.name: The Gentlemen Affiliate Open Directory
infrastructure.description: An open directory discovered by Cisco Talos, believed to be used by an affiliate of The Gentlemen group to store a toolkit with malicious payloads and scripts for attacks against Windows and VMware ESXi.

infrastructure.name: The Gentlemen Data Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A data leak site used by The Gentlemen group to publish exfiltrated victim data as part of their double-extortion strategy.

indicators.name: ESXi VM Kill Command
indicators.pattern:
title: ESXi VM Kill Command via esxcli
id: 2b8a7c1d-e3f4-4b5a-8c6d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'esxcli vm process kill' to terminate virtual machine processes on a VMware ESXi host. This is a common tactic used by ransomware to prepare VMs for encryption.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ransomware-incidents-in-japan-in-the-first-half-of-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/esxcli'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'vm'
      - 'process'
      - 'kill'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the `esxcli vm process kill` command, a technique used by ransomware groups like The Gentlemen to terminate virtual machines before encryption.

indicators.name: ESXi Encryption Script Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential ESXi Ransomware Encryption Script
id: 8d9e0f1a-2b3c-4d5e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of a shell script named 'encrypt.sh' on a Linux-based system, which could be a VMware ESXi host. This filename is commonly associated with ransomware encryption scripts.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ransomware-incidents-in-japan-in-the-first-half-of-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '/encrypt.sh'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of `encrypt.sh`, a potential ransomware script observed in the toolkit of affiliates.

indicators.name: Anomalous SSH to ESXi Host
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous SSH Connection to ESXi Host
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-4a1b-8c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects SSH connections to VMware ESXi hosts originating from non-administrator workstations, which may indicate lateral movement by an attacker.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ransomware-incidents-in-japan-in-the-first-half-of-2026/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1021.004
  - attack.lateral_movement
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort: 22
    DestinationHostname|endswith: 
      - '.esxi.local' # Example, adjust to your environment's naming convention
      - '-esxi'
  filter:
    SourceHostname|startswith:
      - 'admin-ws-'
      - 'jumpbox-'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects SSH connections to ESXi hosts from workstations not designated for administration, a potential indicator of lateral movement.
